channel.title: Ulix Knowledge Briefs
channel.description: Dated notes from Ulix Knowledge on books, research, archives, software, and other developments worth interpreting.

item.title: The 2,500-Year-Old Statue That Became a Paving Stone
item.description: A fifth-century BCE statue survived Roman Sardis because builders broke it up and laid it face down in a street.

item.title: Kusama's Infinity Rooms Did Not Begin With Mirrors
item.description: Before mirrors multiplied Kusama's rooms, she spent years painting and sewing repetition by hand.

item.title: At 10^81 Objects, the Imbalance Is Still About Three
item.description: A new discrepancy bound grows so slowly that even a problem at an absurd physical scale barely moves it.

item.title: An AI Tutor Can Match Retention and Still Lose on Transfer
item.description: Remembering a lesson and using it on a new problem are different achievements.

item.title: Can You Measure “Cognitive Fitness” Like Physical Fitness?
item.description: Three proposed KPIs make cognitive fitness concrete without yet making them validated measures of a generally fitter brain.

item.title: NASA Is Hanging a Fabric Radar Antenna Under a Mars Helicopter
item.description: SkyFall's radar has to see into the top few meters of Mars while its antenna survives being bent under the aircraft every time it lands.

item.title: Why Does Odysseus Cry When He Hears About His Own Victory?
item.description: In Odyssey 8, Homer answers the hero's tears with a simile that puts the conqueror in the place of the conquered.

item.title: The Most Important Thing in This 250-Year Time Capsule May Be the Instructions
item.description: Synthetic DNA may preserve the files until 2276. A decoder chip is there to help make sure somebody can still understand what the files are.

item.title: Juno Just Took Io’s Temperature Beneath the Surface
item.description: An instrument built to peer through Jupiter’s clouds has started measuring heat several meters down in Io’s crust.

item.title: What Makes an AI the Same AI Tomorrow?
item.description: A conversation can outlast the server process and even the model that began it. Memory is starting to shape what counts as continuity in AI systems.

item.title: AI Is Solving Erdős Problems. Counting Them Is the Wrong Ruler.
item.description: The raw count is a bad benchmark. Some of the underlying mathematical results are stronger evidence than the score suggests.

item.title: Good Notes May Work Because They Show You What You Don't Understand
item.description: A new experiment suggests that useful notes may improve learning partly by making overconfidence harder to maintain.

item.title: The First Herculaneum Scroll We Can Read Without Opening
item.description: A sealed Herculaneum papyrus has been virtually unwrapped and read end to end while remaining physically rolled shut.

item.title: Memory Without Provenance Is a Liability
item.description: AI agents are learning to remember. The harder problem is preserving where those memories came from, what surrounded them, and how they changed.

item.title: You Read Differently When You Expect to Remember It
item.description: An eye-tracking study found that reading for study changes what readers actually do with a text. The useful lesson is not simply to read more slowly.

item.title: The Odyssey Is a Bestseller Again. That Is Not a Bad Way to Meet Homer.
item.description: Christopher Nolan's film has sent thousands of readers back to Homer. Whatever one thinks of the adaptation, that is a reasonably good result.
